newsitem.title: USA: Nazis used Swiss diplomatic pouches, document says.
newsitem.headline: Nazis used Swiss diplomatic pouches, document says.

text.p: U.S. diplomats suspected that the Nazis routinely used Swiss diplomatic pouches to send their looted wealth secretly to Argentina during the Second World War, according to a State Department document released on Wednesday.

New York Republican Sen. Alfonse D'Amato released excerpts of the document which detailed the extensive efforts made by Nazi leaders -- including Hermann Goering and Josef Goebbels -- to send their wealth to Argentina, along with an angry letter to Swiss Ambassador Carlo Jagmetti demanding an explanation.

The section of the document that stirred the Senate Banking Committee chairman's wrath was a comment that cited accusations "that Nazi German capital is escaping in Swiss diplomatic pouches, probably without the knowledge of the Swiss federal government because of the government's practice of entrusting diplomatic missions to its bankers and businessmen travelling to the Western World."

D'Amato told the Swiss ambassador in his letter, "I am amazed by a passage in the document which states that Swiss bankers were entrusted to conduct diplomatic missions to South America. My great fear is that it was these bankers who were allowed to carry on such missions that were facilitating the transfer of Nazi loot to Argentina and beyond.

"If this is in fact the case, it is a further indictment of the complicity of Swiss banks in Nazi crimes and must be investigated. I urge you in the strongest of terms to seek answers to these questions and get to the bottom of this explosive issue."

D'Amato's Banking Committee has held hearings on the relationship of Swiss banks to the Nazis during the war and on whether the banks still hold unclaimed wealth from Holocaust victims and looted Nazi assets.

The document the senator released said that the personal fortunes of top Nazi officials like Goering, Goebbels and Robert Ley were reaching Geneva via German diplomatic pouches "and from there -- it is alleged -- they are sent to Buenos Aires."

It added that the "fortunes in securities, bullion and cash transferred to the Argentine capital are only part of the sums being invested abroard for the Nazi hierarchy by banks of neutral countries."

The document said that Goering, Hitler's Reichsmarshal, used diplomatic pouches to send more than $20 million of his "personal fortune to Argentina via the Dresdener Bank of Berlin and the Schweizer Bankverein of Geneva."
Goering also transferred some funds to Argentina by a Nazi submarine in the summer of 1943, according to the document.

It added that Goebbels, Hitler's propaganda chief, had $1.3 million in a safety deposit box in a German-controlled bank in Buenos Aires under the name of a friend, while Foreign Minister Joachim von Ribbentrop had a large sum deposited in a cousin's name in the same bank.
